Changed symbols between two revisions, or in the working tree, with their callers, entry points and labelled candidate tests

Usage: orbit-graph changes [OPTIONS] [RANGE]

Arguments:
  [RANGE]
          Revisions to compare: <base>..<head>, or <base> to compare the working tree against it (default: the working tree against the merge base with the upstream, origin/HEAD, main or master)

Options:
      --symbol <SELECTOR>
          Analyse only this changed symbol (symbol:<path>#<name>:<kind>); repeatable. A selector that matches no changed symbol is listed under unmatched_selection

      --confidence <CONFIDENCE>
          Minimum resolution confidence of every hop (default: same_module). Pass fuzzy to include name-only matches
          
          [default: same_module]
          [possible values: exact, import, same_module, fuzzy]

      --depth <DEPTH>
          Maximum hops from a changed symbol to a caller or entry point (1..=10)
          
          [default: 3]

      --node-cap <NODE_CAP>
          Maximum nodes, and paths, one traversal may return (1..=2000)
          
          [default: 200]

      --query-budget-ms <QUERY_BUDGET_MS>
          Wall-clock budget of one traversal, in milliseconds (100..=60000)
          
          [default: 5000]

      --max-symbols <MAX_SYMBOLS>
          Maximum changed symbols analysed, in changed-symbol order (1..=1000); the rest are listed under not_analysed
          
          [default: 50]

      --max-callers <MAX_CALLERS>
          Maximum callers kept per changed symbol, strongest first (1..=500)
          
          [default: 10]

      --max-entry-points <MAX_ENTRY_POINTS>
          Maximum entry points kept per changed symbol, nearest first (1..=100)
          
          [default: 5]

      --max-tests <MAX_TESTS>
          Maximum candidate tests kept per changed symbol, strongest first (1..=500)
          
          [default: 10]

      --budget-ms <MS>
          Wall-clock budget for the whole run, indexing included, in milliseconds (1000..=3600000; default: none). When it runs out the result is returned with complete: false

      --language <LANGUAGE>
          Keep only changed symbols whose file is in this language

      --scope <PREFIX>
          Keep only changed symbols whose path starts with this prefix

      --cache-dir <DIR>
          Snapshot cache directory (default: <repository>/.orbit-graph/explorer/snapshots)

      --no-cache
          Build snapshots in temporary directories and cache nothing

      --format <MODE>
          Output mode: auto, table, json, or ndjson (default: auto). auto prints a headed table on a terminal but headerless tab-separated rows when piped; use table for a header or json/ndjson for named fields

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Use a table on a terminal and complete plain output otherwise
          - table:  Render the command's human view with headers and terminal adaptation
          - json:   Emit one JSON document
          - ndjson: Emit one complete JSON record per line

      --json
          Shorthand for --format json; combining it with a different --format is an error

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

RANGE is <base>..<head> to compare two revisions, or <base> alone to compare
the working tree (staged, unstaged and untracked files; not ignored ones)
against <base>. Without RANGE the working tree is compared against the merge
base of HEAD and the branch it will land on: its upstream, else origin/HEAD,
else main, else master. Nothing is fetched.

Every caller, entry point and candidate test is labelled with its source
(call_path, import_relationship, reference_path, changed_symbol,
naming_heuristic, runtime_invocation), its evidence category and its
confidence. Candidate tests are what the evidence points at, not proof of
coverage.

Committed snapshots are cached under .orbit-graph/explorer/snapshots in the
repository (graph scratch state), so a second run over the same commits skips
indexing; pass --no-cache to write nothing there. The working tree is never
cached.

Examples:
  orbit-graph changes --json
  orbit-graph changes main..HEAD --json
  orbit-graph changes origin/main --max-tests 20
  orbit-graph changes v1.2.0..v1.3.0 --symbol 'symbol:src/lib.rs#run:function'
